stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt

many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

steps.input: await rlm.harness.create_memory(title="ARC: periodic diagonal stripe fill", content="For ARC grids with sparse straight diagonal colored lines (slope down-right) and blank background, identify each marked diagonal by invariant d = column - row. Treat each distinct colored diagonal track as one entry, including adjacent parallel tracks of same color separately. Let P be the number of marked diagonal tracks. Assign each residue d mod P the marker color seen on that track, then fill the entire grid with the repeating diagonal pattern: output[r][c] = color[(c-r) mod P]. The sequence is diagonal-periodic and constant on down-right diagonals. Verified: 24x24 demo had 5 tracks with residue mapping d mod 5: 0→3, 1→5, 2→9, 3→7, 4→5; output matched. Solved 26x26 instance had four tracks: color3 on d=-9,-8, color4 on d=-2, color5 on d=9; modulo 4 mapping [3,5,4,3], output[r][c] = map[(c-r)%4] was correct. Distinguish diagonal tracks by their d intercepts, not merely distinct colors. Other related ARC setup: horizontal full-width marker bars can encode row-periodic sequences analogously, with residue based on row index; demo output sorted bars by row mod number of tracks.", path="arc")

Do not count only distinct colors: adjacent tracks of one color occupy separate residues. Related case: full-width horizontal marker bars can encode a row-periodic pattern similarly, by row-index residues; demo output sequence corresponds to ordering bar colors by row modulo number of tracks.", path="arc", global_=True)
